sections.title: Klasifikasi Nyeri Kepala

content.text: Headaches are classified into primary headaches (migraine, tension-type, trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias, other primary headaches) and secondary headaches (symptom of another condition). The ICHD-3 (International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition) provides standardized diagnostic criteria.
Nyeri kepala primer: migrain, tension-type, cluster
Nyeri kepala sekunder: gejala kondisi lain

sections.title: Migrain

content.text: Migraine is characterized by recurrent headache attacks lasting 4-72 hours, typically unilateral, pulsating, moderate to severe intensity, aggravated by routine physical activity, and associated with nausea and/or photophobia and phonophobia. MIGRAINE WITH AURA: Recurrent attacks with fully reversible focal neurological symptoms (visual, sensory, speech) that develop gradually over 5-20 minutes and last less than 60 minutes. Visual aura is most common (scintillating scotoma, fortification spectra). MIGRAINE WITHOUT AURA: Most common type (~70-80%). CHRONIC MIGRAINE: Headache on >=15 days/month for >3 months, with migraine features on >=8 days/month.
P-O-U-N-D mnemonic for migraine: Pulsating, duration 4-72h, Unilateral, Nausea, Disabling

sections.title: Red Flags Nyeri Kepala Sekunder

content.text: The SNOOP4 mnemonic helps identify dangerous secondary headaches requiring urgent investigation. S - Systemic symptoms (fever, weight loss, malignancy); N - Neurological signs or symptoms (focal deficit, seizure, papilledema); O - Onset sudden (thunderclap headache - SAH until proven otherwise); O - Older age (>50, especially with temporal artery tenderness - consider giant cell arteritis); P - Pattern change (progressive, different from usual); P - Precipitated by exertion/cough/sex; P - Positional (worse upright suggests CSF leak, worse supine suggests raised ICP); P - Progressive (worsening frequency/severity).
Thunderclap headache = SAH until proven otherwise - immediate CT non-contrast, if negative consider LP for xanthochromia

sections.title: Patofisiologi dan Terapi Akut Migrain

content.text: PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: The trigeminovascular system is central to migraine pathophysiology. Activation of trigeminal nerve fibers innervating meningeal blood vessels releases CGRP (calcitonin gene-related peptide), substance P, and neurokinin A, causing neurogenic inflammation, vasodilation, and pain signal transmission. The brainstem (periaqueductal gray, locus coeruleus) and hypothalamus play modulatory roles. Cortical spreading depression (CSD) is the substrate for migraine aura.

ACUTE TREATMENT: Step 1 - NSAIDs/acetaminophen (mild attacks). Step 2 - Triptans (sumatriptan, rizatriptan) - 5-HT1B/1D agonists, first-line for moderate-severe attacks, contraindicated in cardiovascular disease. Step 3 - Anti-emetics (metoclopramide, prochlorperazine) for nausea and enhancing absorption. Step 4 - Rescue medications (dexamethasone to prevent recurrence). ER protocol: IV metoclopramide + fluids.
Triptans are contraindicated in cardiovascular disease, hemiplegic migraine, and basilar migraine

sections.title: Terapi Preventif Migrain

content.text: INDICATIONS: >=4 migraine days/month, significant disability, frequent use of acute medications (>2 days/week), failure of acute treatment. OPTIONS: Beta-blockers (propranolol, metoprolol); CCBs (flunarizine); Antiepileptics (topiramate, valproate); Tricyclics (amitriptyline); CGRP monoclonal antibodies (erenumab, fremanezumab); Oral CGRP antagonists (rimegepant, atogepant); OnabotulinumtoxinA for chronic migraine.

differential_notes.how_to_separate: Sudden onset 'worst headache of life' - SAH, dissection, pituitary apoplexy; requires emergent CT
Cluster: unilateral orbital, 15-180 min, autonomic symptoms, restless; Migraine: 4-72h, nausea, photophobia, relief with rest
Tension: bilateral, pressing, mild-moderate, no nausea; Migraine: unilateral, pulsating, moderate-severe, with nausea
